key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while higher humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameters should be tuned to minimize coating defects, with service humidity considered when assessing wear performance.
method: Detonation-spray Fe-based amorphous coatings onto Q235 carbon steel under varied spraying parameters.
Characterize droplet morphology and coating microstructure.
Evaluate corrosion and tribological behavior across humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates as humidity increases.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear results involve Si3N4 counterfaces and may not generalize to other contact materials; quantitative performance ranges are not provided in the abstract.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
